body:
It seems that ByteBuddy (which is used by Mockito behind the scenes) won't generate the mock in the same package as the application class because the application class is loaded from the Quarkus ClassLoader.

@stuartwdouglas do you remember why we made Mockito parent first? I am sure there is a really good reason, I just don't remember it :)

So indeed we can't support package-private methods in mocking.

What would a helpful message look like to you @AntonFagerberg ? I mean would you expect to see a warning from Quarkus every time you run the tests warning you that specific methods can't be mocked?
AFAIK it was simply not working when not loaded parent first.

The root cause of this is that QuarkusClassLoader.getParent() does not return the actual parent, but the platform ClassLoader.

This is to work around some really nasty bugs in the MP API artifacts, where they don't leave delegation to the ClassLoader but instead do manual delegation which breaks when you have isolated ClassLoaders (e.g. https://github.com/eclipse/microprofile-reactive-streams-operators/pull/130).
I am testing out https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/compare/master...stuartwdouglas:class-loader-fix?expand=1 to see if there are other problems caused by fixing getParent().

> The root cause of this is that QuarkusClassLoader.getParent() does not return the actual parent, but the platform ClassLoader.
> 
> This is to work around some really nasty bugs in the MP API artifacts, where they don't leave delegation to the ClassLoader but instead do manual delegation which breaks when you have isolated ClassLoaders (e.g. [eclipse/microprofile-reactive-streams-operators#130](https://github.com/eclipse/microprofile-reactive-streams-operators/pull/130)).

Wow! I didn't even consider this :)
I had no idea we used the _platform_ classloader as the parent in order to get around MP issues...
Furthemore, debugging output for the TCCL (which of course is a Quarkus ClassLoader) had tricked me into a false sense of complacency 🤦🏼 (as I saw the parent _field_ properly set)

> The root cause of this is that QuarkusClassLoader.getParent() does not return the actual parent, but the platform ClassLoader.
> 

Now that is one thing I won't be forgetting anytime soon 😆
Once we have a new reactive streams operations API release we should be able to remove the hack

null, and fixes it with some smaller more limited hacks around the
problematic API's.

Fixes #14898
